doc.title: Will Shade and Dewey Corley Interview, 1960-05-25

title: What became of Memphis Minnie, Frank Stokes, Jim Jackson and Furry Lewis
summary: Shade reports Minnie's stroke, the deaths of Stokes, Dan Sane and Jim Jackson, and that Furry Lewis lives close by.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And you said Memphis Minnie was here now, huh?

Memphis Minnie is sick. She got a stroke. She can't talk, can't walk in a wheelchair. Gee, that's terrible. Her husband also is the same way. He got a stroke. Got a stroke way before she did. The first of the winter.
And Frank Stokes and Dan Sane, what happened to them?
They died. Both of them is dead.
Gee. What did Jim Jackson feature?
Well, he played the Kansas City Blues and some other different blues. I never did keep up with them much.
Oh, he played the ghetto already. I didn't know he played that.
Furry Lewis, he played guitar. Made a record for Wildback. John Hen wrote a vocation. Some other songs he had to play but I didn't know the rest of the titles of them.
Well, I'm glad to hear he's around. I'm sorry we don't have time to look him up.
Well, he ain't so far, man. He's just about five or ten blocks from here. Take a long drive around that city state. You could pick him up anytime. He'd be glad to see you.
We'll catch him on the next trip. Maybe you'll see him in the meantime and can get his address.
